prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1467; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a collision at an intersection where the insured was turning left and was struck in the side by an oncoming vehicle. The claimant's attorney has written to confirm representation and asks that all contact be directed through their office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact and records the scene as consistent with the reported left turn. Photos taken at the scene show the damage pattern and confirm several of the details the insured described.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided a summary of injuries including a fracture to the wrist. The injury appears consistent in type and force with a side impact of this kind.

Entry 4: Contacted the claimant, who gave the same account of the collision as in the first notice, describing the left turn and the moment of impact. The account has not changed across each contact so far.

Entry 5: Requested medical records. Initial treatment followed a usual course for this type of fracture, with care tapering off as the claimant's condition improved.

Entry 6: Medical history shows a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which healed fully with no lasting problems. Noted for review, though it does not appear to change the current injury picture.

Entry 7: Canvassed the intersection for independent witnesses. None were located, so the claim relies on the police report, scene photos, and the parties' accounts.

Entry 8: Reviewed the vehicle file. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the records suggests the damage predates the policy's effective date.

Entry 9: Confirmed the driver is a member of the policyholder's household and is covered under the policy as a household member. Coverage questions have been resolved on this point.

Entry 10: Reviewing whether all of the claimed damage came from this impact. It is not yet clear how much of the treatment and vehicle damage is attributable to this collision, and the file remains open pending a further review with the attorney.
